title: Administrative Assistant
description:
What you'll do
The CERN Staff Association (SA) is committed to promoting the welfare of CERN personnel through a wide range of services and initiatives. Among these is the Jardin des Particules (JDP), an early childhood education and childcare facility located at CERN, welcoming children from 4 months to 10 years old.
We are looking for an experienced Administrative Assistant to play a central role in the day-to-day administration and management of the Jardin des Particules. This is a varied position combining human resources administration, financial management and operational coordination within a Swiss employment framework.
If you enjoy taking ownership of diverse administrative responsibilities, have solid knowledge of Swiss employment administration and thrive in an international environment, then join the CERN Staff Association and contribute to an essential service for the CERN community.
Learn more
Your responsibilities
Managing the full administrative lifecycle of JDP employees, including recruitment administration, employment contracts, amendments, onboarding and departures.
Coordinating payroll administration with the external fiduciary and ensuring the accuracy of salary-related information.
Managing personnel administration in accordance with Swiss employment legislation, including social insurance, pension schemes (LPP), employment contracts, leave management and other statutory obligations.
Acting as the main administrative contact for JDP staff on employment-related matters.
Monitoring the JDP budget, processing invoices and payments, maintaining accounting records and supporting financial reporting.
Performing financial monitoring and analysis to support sound budget management.
Liaising with external partners including the fiduciary, insurance providers and public authorities when required.
Preparing communication and promotional material for the Jardin des Particules and supporting its visibility within the CERN community.
Contributing to the continuous improvement of administrative and financial processes.
In addition, you will provide occasional support to the Staff Association Secretariat by welcoming visitors and responding to general enquiries.
Still here?
Let's make a quick check about
Your profile
Demonstrated experience managing employment administration under Swiss labour legislation, including employment contracts, payroll administration, social insurance, occupational pension schemes (LPP) and other statutory employment obligations.
Proven experience in administrative, HR and financial administration within a small or medium-sized enterprise (SME) in Switzerland.
Experience working with external fiduciaries or payroll providers would be an asset.
Experience in an international or multicultural environment would be an advantage.
Technical Certificate or General Secondary Education or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Administration, Human Resources, Accounting, Finance or a related field.
Your skills
Secretarial work.
Use of office software packages.
Knowledge of accounting software, such as Crésus, would be an asset.
Accounting, budget monitoring and financial control.
Administration of employment contracts and personnel records under Swiss employment legislation.
Gains trust and collaboration from others.
Ensures that information, procedures and decisions are appropriately documented.
Works conscientiously and reliably; delivers on promises.
Relates well to all people regardless of category/level within the Organization.
Adapts quickly and resourcefully to shifting priorities and requirements.
Spoken and written both English and French.
Global Benefits at CERN
A minimum net entry-salary of 5929 Swiss Francs per month, increasing in line with your years of relevant experience.
30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.
Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.
Family, child and infant monthly allowances depending on your individual circumstances.
A relocation package (installation grant, removal, travel expenses) depending on your individual circumstances.
Possibility to extend your contract up to 8 years + eligibility for indefinite contract tenure.
Let's get you ready
Be sure to meet the eligibility criteria
You are a national of a CERN Member State or Associate Member State. Currently, we cannot consider applications from Pakistani, Lithuanian, Latvian, Cypriot, Croatian and Turkish nationals, as the ceiling defined under Article II.5 of the Associate Membership Agreement has been reached.
You have relevant qualifications and professional experience.
If you have previously held a Staff contract at CERN, you will not be eligible for these positions.
Please pay attention to the additional criteria and requirements for this specific position and mentioned above.
You will need these documents to complete your application
Your CV (English or French)
Any document you consider relevant to your application
Your CERNDepartment

Discover a world where the impossible is made possible!
At CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, we are pushing the frontiers of science and technology. Our groundbreaking work brings together not only physicists but also a diverse range of professionals from engineering, technical, scientific, and administrative fields. Together, we foster an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive.
Every day, we face exciting new challenges and opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research that shapes our understanding of the universe. We meet these challenges through the diverse perspectives within our teams, ensuring every contribution is valued and driving our shared sense of inclusion and purpose. Diversity is a core value of CERN since its foundation, and it remains central to our mission and continued success.
If you are ready to be part of a dynamic, inclusive community pushing the boundaries of knowledge, CERN is the place where your curiosity and skills can thrive. Be part of our mission to uncover what lies at the heart of the universe! TAKE PART!

What should I expect during my first week at CERN?

Your onboarding at CERN includes a comprehensive induction programme, which starts with an official welcome session at the beginning of each month. In addition, you will receive important information both before and after your arrival to ensure a smooth transition into your new role. This process is designed to help you get acquainted with CERN’s environment, your team, and the tools and systems you’ll be using.
How big would the team be?

The size of the team you'll be working with at CERN depends on the specific role and department. Some teams are small and highly specialized, while others are larger and more interdisciplinary. During the interview process, you'll have the opportunity to learn more about the team structure for the position you are applying for.
What is the working language at CERN?

The working languages at CERN are English and French. However, it is not always mandatory to speak both languages to work at CERN. We offer language training to help you acquiring the other language.
What support does CERN provide for relocation?

CERN does not offer direct assistance with relocation. However, depending on your role and specific criteria, you may be eligible for certain benefits such as an installation allowance and coverage of travel expenses to join CERN. These benefits are designed to help ease the transition when relocating to the Geneva area. For more information, please consult the “Salary, Benefits and Support“ page.
Do I need a visa to work at CERN?

Whether you need a visa to work at CERN depends on your nationality and the duration of your stay. CERN assists with the necessary visa and work permit processes for its employees and visitors. The specific requirements will be communicated to you during the recruitment process.
What would my salary be?

Salaries at CERN are determined by a structured scale. Salaries are based on your role, qualifications, and experience, and are not subject to negotiation. Specific details will be provided as your application progresses. For more information, please refer to the dedicated page.

title: Administrative Assistant
description:
What you'll do
As an Administrative Assistant in the CERN Users Office, you will contribute to the delivery of customer-focused administrative services for CERN’s international community of guest scientists, supporting processes related to registration, personnel formalities, and Host State documentation. You will gain hands-on experience in administrative coordination, stakeholder engagement, and service delivery while contributing to the implementation of CERN’s new Human Capital Management (HCM) system and the development of onboarding initiatives that support the integration of newcomers across the Administration Directorate.
Your responsibilities
Provide administrative support and guidance to CERN's guest scientists, facilitating registration, personnel formalities, and their integration into the CERN community.
Process, maintain, and manage administrative records and documentation, ensuring data quality and accuracy across CERN's information systems.
Contribute to the continuous delivery of administrative services by supporting team activities and ensuring service continuity when required.
Support the documentation, review, and improvement of administrative and Human Capital Management (HCM) processes, including the collection and analysis of user feedback.
Contribute to the development and maintenance of onboarding resources, communication materials, and knowledge-sharing initiatives that support the successful integration of newcomers across AGS services.

Initial experience in administrative support, customer service, office administration, or a related field would be considered an asset.

Experience maintaining records, documentation, or administrative information would be considered an asset.
Familiarity with standard office software and digital collaboration tools.
Exposure to onboarding activities, user support, feedback collection, or the preparation of guidance materials would be an advantage.
Your studies focused on General Administration, Customer Service.
Your skills
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively in an international and multicultural environment.
Service-oriented mindset and ability to interact professionally with a diverse range of stakeholders.
Good organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks, maintain accurate records, and follow up on activities.
Strong attention to detail and ability to handle information, documentation, and data with accuracy and confidentiality.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and collaborative document management tools.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.

title: Applied Physicist – ATLAS Muon LS3 Integration and Installation Manager
description:
What you'll do
As ATLAS Muon LS3 Integration and Installation Manager you will play a key role in the preparation and execution of activities during Long Shutdown 3 (LS3). You will be responsible for ensuring effective coordination across all ATLAS Muon sub-projects. You will closely follow daily work at P1 for Muon upgrade and maintenance projects, monitor progress, and take action to keep Muon activities on schedule. The role requires close collaboration with various ATLAS Muon sub-projects, ATLAS Technical Coordination (TC), and other relevant CERN groups. You will serve as the primary interface between the Muon projects and ATLAS TC, ensuring coherent planning, efficient execution, and comprehensive reporting of all activities.

During Long Shutdown 3 (LS3, 2026–2030), the ATLAS Muon detector will undergo significant upgrades, including the installation of new detector systems and extensive maintenance of existing detector components. As the ATLAS Muon LS3 Integration and Installation Manager, you will play a central role in planning, coordinating, and monitoring these activities.
Your responsibilities
Responsible for ensuring effective coordination of installation and integration activities across the Muon projects, tracking progress, identifying risks, and ensuring effective communication among all participating teams.
Act as the liaison between the various Muon sub-projects and ATLAS TC, providing regular status updates and comprehensive documentation.
Develop, maintain, and monitor the integrated LS3 schedule for Muon installation, integration, and maintenance activities in close collaboration with ATLAS TC team.
Coordinate and oversee technical activities on the ATLAS Muon detectors in the UX15 cavern.
Identify, manage, and resolve interface issues, schedule conflicts, and resource constraints across multiple projects and teams.
Organise and chair regular ATLAS Muon LS3 coordination meetings, collect status information, and maintain an overview of ongoing and planned activities.
Support Muon detector teams in coordinating LS3 activities to ensure timely delivery and efficient planning.
Prepare and maintain comprehensive documentation, progress reports, and activity summaries.

Let's make a quick check about
Your profile
Proven experience in coordinating activities for large-scale detector systems or comparable complex scientific installations.
Demonstrated experience in planning and managing work program involving multiple teams and stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience coordinating complex technical projects, managing competing priorities, and resolving planning, scheduling, and resource constraints in a multidisciplinary environment.
Experience with safety systems and safety-related technical infrastructure.
Familiarity with installation, integration, commissioning, or maintenance activities in large scientific facilities is considered an asset.
PhD or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Physics or a related field.
Your skills
Assembly and integration of detectors.
Knowledge and application of gas based particle detection technologies.
Testing and validation of detector, accelerator and beam line components.
Assembly and integration of infrastructure for detectors or experimental facilities.
Organisation, planning and control.
Team management.
Uses openness and honesty to interact constructively with others.
Adapts quickly and resourcefully to shifting priorities and requirements.
Produces workable and timely solutions that meet requirements.
Takes initiative beyond regular tasks and makes things happen.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Medical hazard
Exposure to electromagnetic fields under certain conditions.
Employment conditions
Work in Radiation Areas.
Interventions in underground installations.
A valid driving licence.
Work during nights, Sundays and official holidays, when required by the needs of the Organization.

title: Applied Physicist/Engineer - ATLAS ITk
description:
What you'll do
The CERN ATLAS Team plays a major role in the construction of the future silicon ATLAS Inner Tracker (ITk). In particular, the final integration of the ITk detector prior to installation in the experiment is a crucial step to validate the full functionality.

As an applied physicist or engineer in the CERN-ATL Team, you will join the Tracker section (EP-ATL-TRK) and work closely with personnel from the Detector Technologies Group (EP-DT) on the construction and integration of the ATLAS ITk Pixel System and its integration into the ATLAS ITk.
Your responsibilities
Reception testing of ITk Silicon Pixel Detector elements and testing of multi-module Pixel structures to be integrated into the ITk Pixel Outer Barrel.
Testing and verification of integrated ITk Pixel Detector structures and services as well as combined testing with the ITk Strip Detector in the surface integration facility (SR1) at CERN.
Deploy and improve software and hardware elements for integration testing and service validation (online, detector control, detector safety) for the Pixel Detector and the combined ITk.
Document procedures and results for ITk integration testing and service validation and develop testing procedures for the ITk Detector after installation.
Participate hands-on in the ITk Detector integration work in the surface cleanroom as well as the preparation of equipment for the different testing stages.
Still here?
Let's make a quick check about
Your profile
Proven experience in the construction and integration of silicon pixel detectors for high energy physics experiments.
Proven experience in the testing and data analysis of silicon detector systems.
Proven experience in silicon detector operation and quality control including the development, installation and commissioning of laboratory infrastructure.
Experience in the development of DAQ/online software or detector control systems for silicon detector testing and operation.
Demonstrated experience in working in a multi-disciplinary team and international collaboration, including physicists, engineers and technicians involved in work on detector construction.
Experience on interpreting CAD designs of mechanics components or cooling plant operation is advantageous.
Experience with the assembly of sensitive equipment in a clean room environment is advantageous.
Master's degree or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Applied Physicist or Engineering or a related field.
Your skills
Testing and validation of detector, accelerator and beam line components.
Assembly and integration of detectors.
Construction, test and installation of electromechanical equipment and systems.
Development of application software.
Assembly and integration of infrastructure for detectors or experimental facilities.
Delivers high quality work on time and fulfils expectations.
Adapts quickly and resourcefully to shifting priorities and requirements.
Builds and maintains constructive and effective work relationships.
Works well autonomously; takes on activities and tasks without prompting.
Expresses opinions, ideas and suggestions with conviction and in a logical/structured manner; keeps to the point.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Employment conditions
A valid driving licence.
Work in Radiation Areas.
Interventions in underground installations.
Work during nights, Sundays and official holidays, when required by the needs of the Organization.

title: Controls and Automation Engineer
description:
What you'll do
The Engineering Department (EN) pushes the boundaries of technology to enable physicists to carry out world-class scientific research. Within the EN Department, the Cooling and Ventilation Group (EN-CV) is responsible for the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of the cooling and ventilation installations that support CERN’s accelerators, experimental facilities, and technical infrastructure.
Within EN-CV, the Controls Section (EN-CV-CL) is responsible for the specification, development, commissioning, operation, and maintenance of the industrial control systems used across all EN-CV installations.
The EN-CV control systems are based on industrial technologies, including Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems, the UNICOS framework developed at CERN, automated code generation tools, and virtual commissioning methodologies. More than 650 PLCs are currently deployed and operated across EN-CV facilities, requiring a very high level of reliability, availability, and maintainability.
As a Controls Engineer, you will be involved in the full lifecycle of industrial control systems, from defining requirements and technical specifications to designing and implementing control solutions.

Define control system requirements and produce functional specifications for cooling and ventilation installations.

title: Distributed Storage Engineer
description:
What you'll do
Work with us to evolve the CERN data storage systems used at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and at its international partners. CERN is the birthplace of the World Wide Web and one of the world’s leading laboratories for particle physics. Join the Storage and Data Management Group in CERN’s IT Department as a Distributed Storage Engineer for a unique challenge as the next step in your career. CERN, take part! The CERN IT Storage and Data Management group operates the core services used by both LHC and non-LHC experiments for data collection, archival, reconstruction, analysis, and global distribution via the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid. Join us to work on core data storage and management capabilities which enable scientific progress at CERN!
As a Distributed Storage Engineer, you will contribute to the design, evolution, and operation of large-scale, distributed critical storage services for the CERN cloud and computing infrastructures. You will join a team to work with open-source Ceph-based block, object, and filesystem solutions (including CephFS and NFS integrations), ensuring high availability, performance, and resilience across multi-datacenter environments.
Your role will involve system-wide troubleshooting in a distributed Linux-based environment and optimising storage architectures for demanding workloads. You will use your C++ software development skills to help identify and troubleshoot issues with the Ceph code base and to contribute code improvements to the upstream open-source Ceph project when necessary.
You will have opportunities to learn and contribute to improving automation, deployment, and observability, aligned with modern DevOps practices, to participate in inspiring projects and new technologies such as storage for HPC and AI/ML and to engage with our international partners, participating to conferences and workshops.
Your responsibilities
Management and operations of distributed disk storage, block, object and filesystem services based on mainstream open-source technologies (Ceph)
Participate in the evolution of architecture and design of storage services for CERN and software-defined storage technology with Open Source
Integrate, troubleshoot and maintain distributed disk storage systems at scale, across multiple availability zones and data centres.
Contribute to documentation, development, optimisation and further automation of storage services
Contribute to change management, incident response, and user support.
Liaise with key stakeholders inside and outside of the IT department.

Debugging and diagnosing issues in complex distributed environments, spanning hardware, network, and software layer
Demonstrated experience in C++ software development of distributed storage systems (preferably, but not necessarily, with Ceph source code)
Strong collaboration and communication skills to work effectively with multiple cross-functional teams, users and partners.
Master's degree or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Computer Science or a related field.
Your skills
Design of storage systems.
Development of application software.
Knowledge of programming techniques and languages.
Knowledge of storage technologies.
Operation and maintenance (preventive and corrective) of storage systems.
Delivers prompt and efficient service taking into account customer needs.
Readily absorbs new techniques and working practices; proposes new or improved ways of working.
Seeks and integrates other points of view when tackling an issue; consults experts in the field and undertakes benchmarking.
Builds and maintains constructive and effective work relationships.
Seeks feedback from colleagues and other stakeholders about ways of increasing competence.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.

Stand-by duty, when required by the needs of the Organization.

Help shape the future of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) machine protection systems. We are looking for a motivated Engineer to contribute to the renovation of the LHC Collimator Control System, a critical component ensuring the safe and reliable operation of the world’s most powerful particle accelerator. Working in a highly collaborative environment you will help to increase the reliability, usability, and long-term maintainability of systems at the heart of LHC operations. Coordinate and support control system commissioning, performing functional testing, validation, and verification of interlocks and fail-safes prior to operational deployment.
Integrate control systems with the alarm server and develop high-level tools to enhance usability and real-time monitoring.

Support expert and operational interfaces, providing diagnostic capabilities and improving intervention workflows.

The SY-BI group in CERN’s Accelerator Systems Department develops and operates the instruments used to observe particle beams and measure their key properties. These systems are essential to the reliable operation, optimisation, and future development of CERN’s accelerator complex.
You will contribute to the development of next-generation beam-position monitoring systems for CERN’s injector complex, including the pre-accelerators and Antimatter Decelerator. Within the framework of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider project, and long shutdown activities, you will join the Cryogenic Group as a full member of the team, working in a multidisciplinary environment focused on cryogenic instrumentation, control systems, and electrical engineering. Collaborating within multidisciplinary teams and contributing to the training and supervision of students.

title: Laser Scientist ISOLDE RILIS
description:
What you'll do
The Resonance Ionisation Laser Ion Source (RILIS), ISOLDE’s principal ion source, is being consolidated after over 30 years of operation. The laboratory housing the laser installation has been dismantled and is being rebuild with a larger footprint and improved safety. With ISOLDE aiming to deliver beams again in summer of 2028 to its user community of >1000 scientists from across the world, we are looking for an experienced person who will help us to reinstall the laser system and recommission it for ion beam generation.
Your responsibilities
Install the lasers as well as the required hard- and software to operate the RILIS on a 24/7 basis with automated laser beam stabilisation and monitoring.
Test the new pump lasers.
Develop new resonance ionisation schemes, targeted at moving RILIS into a fully solid-state laser laboratory.
Document the laser system, creating a detailed operational requirement specification.
Participate in set up and operation of the laser ion source including on-call operational duties.

Demonstrated experience in the installation, commissioning and operation of complex laser systems.

Experience with ion sources, accelerator facilities or large-scale scientific infrastructures is advantageous.
Experience with vacuum systems, instrumentation, safety systems or machine operation is advantageous.
Familiarity with high-availability research facilities supporting user programmes is advantageous.
Your studies focused on Physics, Applied Physics, Photonics, Engineering.

Proven ability to diagnose and solve complex technical problems in experimental environments.
Ability to work both independently and as part of an international multidisciplinary team.
Knowledge of resonance ionisation spectroscopy is advantageous.

Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.

Exposure to carcinogens, mutagens or agents toxic to reproduction.

description:

As a Mechanical CAD Designer in the Superconducting Magnet Technology section, you will develop three-dimensional computer-aided design (CAD) models and detailed drawings for novel superconducting magnets and associated tooling. Working closely with engineers and other technical specialists, you will take part in research and development projects for future particle accelerators. Your work will help transform innovative magnet concepts into manufacturable prototypes and practical assembly solutions.
Learn more
Your responsibilities
Prepare 3D CAD mechanical models and drawings of short magnet demonstrators, prototypes and associated tooling, in close collaboration with other colleagues in the section.
Update CAD models and drawings to integrate feedback from construction and assembly activities.
Contribute to technical discussions related to mechanical tolerances, machining methods and assembly procedures.
Support procurement of components and update CAD models and drawings to reflect as-built configurations.
Assist colleagues with tailored 3D models for computer numerical control (CNC) machining and simulations (electromagnetic, mechanical).
Still here?
Let's make a quick check about

Proficiency in CATIA (or a similar modern 3D CAD software), including the production of detailed 2D manufacturing and assembly drawings, for mechanical components and assemblies.
Experience with a Product Lifecycle Management database (e.g. PLM, Enovia, SmarTeam) to manage models and drawings.
Knowledge of mechanical assemblies and ISO-GPS dimensioning and tolerancing.
Knowledge of superconducting magnet construction and technologies would be an asset.
Higher technical diploma or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Mechanical Engineering or a related field.
Your skills
Knowledge and application of manufacturing methods and work preparation.
Assembly of mechanical structures and equipment.
Production of 2D drawings and 3D models.
Knowledge and application of mechanical measurement techniques.
Works well in groups and readily fits into a team; participates fully and takes an active role in team activities.
Works conscientiously and reliably; delivers on promises.
Adapts quickly and resourcefully to shifting priorities and requirements.
Shares knowledge and expertise freely and willingly with others.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language.

A valid driving licence.
Stand-by duty, when required by the needs of the Organization.

title: Mechanical Engineer for Vacuum Technology

Join CERN’s Vacuum, Surfaces and Coatings Group and contribute to engineering projects supporting the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments. As a Mechanical Engineer in the Experimental Vacuum team, you will work on the design, development, production and testing of ultra-high vacuum equipment around the ATLAS, ALICE, CMS and LHCb experiments. You will take part in projects from initial engineering concepts through design, simulation and prototyping to testing, installation and operational follow-up. Working alongside engineers, technicians and specialists from other disciplines, you will gain hands-on experience with complex mechanical systems in a unique scientific environment.
Your responsibilities
Design and develop precision mechanical equipment for ultra-high vacuum applications.
Create 3D CAD models and perform structural, thermal and modal analyses to validate designs.
Follow projects through design, prototyping, manufacturing, assembly and testing.
Plan and carry out laboratory tests, including leak detection, residual gas analysis and vacuum performance measurements.
Work with CERN workshops, suppliers and technical teams to support production and quality control.

Collaborate across engineering disciplines to solve technical challenges and deliver reliable solutions.

Good foundation in mechanical engineering and design.

Practical, curious and solution-oriented approach.

title: Mechanical Technician for CMS
description:
What you'll do
We are recruiting two early-career graduates for Mechanical Technician positions within the CMS experiment. Both positions involve hands-on mechanical work and close collaboration with technicians, engineers, and physicists, but each will have a different main area of responsibility:
– One position will join the Electromagnetic Calorimeter (ECAL) team, supporting the refurbishment of the barrel electromagnetic calorimeter and covering a large panel of activities and responsibilities, from mechanical work and the handling and assembly of detector parts to logistic activities.
– The second position will join the CMS Technical Coordination crew, supporting mechanical activities for the CMS detector and its infrastructure, including maintenance, upgrades, tooling, and heavy-lifting operations.
Your responsibilities
Within the ECAL team, you will participate in the extraction and insertion of the ECAL supermodules, including the preparation, installation, and removal of the required tooling.
Within the ECAL team, you will carry out mechanical operations during the refurbishment of the supermodules, including the replacement of cooling fittings.
Within the ECAL team, you will support the installation of ECAL services and electronics and assist with related logistics.
Within the CMS Technical Coordination team, you will participate in mechanical work for the upgrade, maintenance, and repair of the CMS detector and its associated infrastructure.
Within the CMS Technical Coordination team, you will manufacture mechanical parts and contribute to on-site assembly, installation, alignment, and repair activities.
Within the CMS Technical Coordination team, you will support the development of tooling and the preparation or modification of technical drawings using drafting software such as CATIA.
Within the CMS Technical Coordination team, you will participate in heavy-lifting and movement operations using equipment such as strand jacks, air pads, and hydraulic jacks, and support regular checks and maintenance of this equipment.

title: NGT Communications Officer
description:
What you'll do
Are you a motivated communications professional with experience in scientific communication for a wide range of audiences – from technical to the project stakeholders as well as the general public? Would you like to join the team responsible for sharing the excitement of Next Generation Triggers (NGT) Project, activities, and collaborative work, with the outside world? Are you skilled at producing scientific materials across a variety of media (social media, videos, printed documents, web pages, etc.) and in organising events? Take part!
The Next Generation Triggers project, or NextGen, started in January 2024 as a collaboration between CERN (the Experimental Physics, Theoretical Physics and Information Technology Departments) and the ATLAS and CMS experiments. The key objective of the five-year NextGen project is to get more physics information out of the HL-LHC data. The hope is to uncover as-yet-unseen phenomena by more efficiently selecting interesting physics events while rejecting background noise. Scientists will make use of advanced algorithmic and computational approaches, from AI/ML to FPGAs, to improve the theoretical modelling and optimise their tools in the search for ultra-rare events.
Your responsibilities
Develop and implement NGT strategic communication plan, ensuring alignment with CERN IT, CERN openlab, ATLAS, CMS and central communications rules.
Plan, create and coordinate social media content and communication campaigns for dissemination across CERN, CERN Computing, ATLAS, CMS and other relevant channels, working with the corresponding communication teams.
Develop, manage and evolve NGT's website, ensuring high-quality content, strong visual identity, and effective user experience.
Plan, create, and analyse social media campaigns from editorial planning to performance reporting, using appropriate multimedia and analytics tools.
Conceptualise and produce high-quality publications and visual materials (annual reports, brochures, leaflets, promotional items) using professional design tools such as InDesign and Illustrator.
Act as the communication interface between CERN NGT management, NGT stakeholders and CERN central communication teams.
Support and manage the communication of the CERN STEAM Academy, including its website and digital content, promotion, lecture programme, student communications and related activities.
Support the communication surrounding NGT workshops and other events, including participant communications, promotional content and related tasks.

As a Software Developer, you will contribute to the upgrade of the CMS data acquisition system for the High-Luminosity LHC. You will design and develop software for FPGA-based electronics platforms, enabling the configuration, control and monitoring of the Trigger and Timing Control and Distribution System (TCDS). Working closely with electronics engineers, physicists and other stakeholders, you will contribute to requirements gathering, the production of detailed documentation, and direct participation in the preparation and execution of system tests at progressively larger scales, in view of deploying the production system in 2028.

In collaboration with other members of the group and CMS collaborators, develop software to configure, control, and monitor the different components of the TCDS system. This requires close interaction with hardware components.
Contribute to the setup and operation of DAQ test systems to validate the different parts of the design.
Maintain and improve software repositories and Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) infrastructure.
Contribute to the installation and commissioning of the Phase-2 DAQ system between 2027 and 2029.

Proficiency in Python and modern C++.
Proven background in collaborative software development and DevOps practices.
Practical experience with web UI development using JavaScript, TypeScript, and related modern frameworks.

title: Particle Accelerator Operator
description:
What you'll do
We invite you to take your career to an exciting new level by joining the team of operators who run the CERN accelerator complex from the CERN Control Centre (CCC). The Operations Group is responsible for the exploitation of the entire CERN accelerator complex and its technical infrastructure, including the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), running a rich proton, antiproton and heavy ion experimental programme. You will be at the heart of the preparation and delivery of particle beams to the different physics programs at CERN. When not operating these complex machines, you will contribute to the development of applications and advanced tools to support and improve operation.
Learn more
Your responsibilities
Take part in the 24/7 shift team which runs CERN's accelerator complex.
Operate proton and/or ion accelerators (Linac3, Linac4, PSB, LEIR and/or PS) and the beam lines to the associated experimental facilities on a shift basis, ensuring the safe and timely execution of the physics schedule and obtaining the defined beam performance goals.
Work closely with accelerator physicists to set up and optimise the accelerator operation and to design, document, commission and optimise various operational scenarios.
Participate in the development of applications and advanced tools as part of a team or in collaboration with engineers or physicists within the OP group or within a specialised equipment group.
Outside periods of accelerator operation, assist the technical infrastructure team with the operation of CERN's technical infrastructure or other CERN equipment groups, if required.
Still here?
Let's make a quick check about
Your profile
Initial work experience in a technical or scientific environment.
Experience in the field of physics, engineering or computing.
Basic knowledge of software engineering in a modern development language environment.
Familiarity with automation concepts and techniques, with an interest in improving operational efficiency and reliability.
Drive to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team and contribute to continuous operational improvements.
Experience in the field of operating large facilities and their associated hardware (e.g. measurement devices, power converter techniques, vacuum equipment, PLCs, work in controlled radiation areas, etc.) would be an asset.
Higher Technical or Administrative Diploma or equivalent in the field of Administration, Computer Engineering, Data Analysis (non-exhaustive) or a related field.
Your skills
Operation of accelerators.
Analysis and optimization of accelerator performance.
Testing and validation of detector, accelerator and beam line components.
Knowledge of programming techniques and languages.
Development of application software.
Cooperates constructively with others in the pursuit of team goals; balances personal goals with team goals.
Takes initiative beyond regular tasks and makes things happen.
Anticipates obstacles; assesses alternative solutions in order to have a fall-back plan.
Ensures that information, procedures and decisions are appropriately documented.
Takes responsibility for own actions and decisions.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language.
Medical hazard
Shift work.
Given the occupational health risks associated with this position, the selected candidate must obtain medical clearance before a contract offer is confirmed.
Employment conditions
A valid driving licence.
Shift work, including nights, Sundays and official holidays.

A minimum net entry-salary of 5929 Swiss Francs per month, increasing in line with your years of relevant experience.
30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.
Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.

title: Planning Engineer
description:
What you'll do
As a Planning Engineer within the ATLAS Technical Coordination, you will play a key role in monitoring ATLAS activities during Long Shutdown 3 (LS3). You will be responsible for keeping the installation schedule up to date, reporting any delays, and proposing mitigation measures to recover lost time. The ATLAS schedule is a complex construction programme encompassing several sub-projects. You will collaborate closely with the various Project Engineers and Project Leaders to understand their constraints and support them in implementing any necessary changes to the schedule baseline. You will also join the Project Management Office (PMO) and play a leading role in the preparation of the quarterly status report, assisting the Upgrade Project Leaders in updating the schedule and reporting on progress.
Your responsibilities
Develop and maintain the ATLAS installation schedules for Long Shutdown 3 (LS3), and actively participate in all schedule baseline changes resulting from the evolution of the LS3 programme.
Monitor and review the progress of activities during planning meetings and in close collaboration with Project Engineers.
Report any delays to the Technical Coordination Management and propose mitigation measures to recover lost time.
Contribute to the maintenance and continuous improvement of the scheduling tools.
Play a leading role in the quarterly status reporting process for the Phase-2 Upgrade projects, and assist the Upgrade Project Leaders in preparing updated schedules, progress reports, and schedule baseline changes.
Supervise the ATLAS team responsible for developing and maintaining the interface with the ATLAS Oracle database. Collect requirements for the evolution of the existing ATLAS information-management tools and establish priorities for the maintenance and development activities of the small team of software engineers.

Demonstrated experience in planning, forecasting, and resource coordination, preferably in an engineering environment, together with strong knowledge of relevant planning software (e.g. MS Project).
Experience liaising with internal and external stakeholders.
Initial experience in coordinating technical activities.
Experience with databases and interfacing tools is an asset.
Experience in team supervision is considered an advantage.
Master's degree or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Engineering, preferably in Mechanical, Industrial, Civil, or Systems Engineering, or a related field.

Organisation, planning and control.
Project management.
Assembly and integration of infrastructure for detectors or experimental facilities.
Implementation of vision and strategic agility.
Delivers high quality work on time and fulfils expectations.
Builds and maintains constructive and effective work relationships.
Works well autonomously; takes on activities and tasks without prompting.
Recognises what is essential; discriminates between important and peripheral information and is able to see the whole picture.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.

Work in Radiation Areas.
Interventions in underground installations.

title: Research Fellowship: Theoretical Physics
description:
What you'll do
You will join one of CERN’s theoretical physics research groups, if selected for this Research Fellowship, to develop and lead your own research programme at the frontier of fundamental physics. You will work in a highly collaborative and international environment, contributing to the development of theoretical models, performing analytical and computational research, and advancing the understanding of particle physics and related fields.
You will also be part of CERN’s vibrant scientific community through seminars, workshops, training activities and collaborative projects.
Your responsibilities
You conduct research in theoretical physics.
You contribute to CERN’s theoretical physics programme by developing innovative theoretical approaches and advancing the interpretation of experimental results.
You collaborate with theoretical and experimental physicists on research related to particle physics and fundamental interactions.
You develop and pursue your own research interests within the framework of the Fellowship.
Still here?
Let's make a quick check about
Your profile
You hold a PhD in theoretical physics or have a scheduled PhD defence before taking up your appointment at CERN.
You have no more than six years of research experience after completing your PhD.
You have a strong background in theoretical particle physics or a closely related field.
You have research experience aligned with the scientific activities carried out within CERN’s Theory Department.
You are motivated to join a leading international research environment and contribute to high-impact scientific research.
You are eager to develop and pursue your own research interests within the Fellowship framework.
Your skills
You have strong analytical and problem-solving skills in the context of theoretical physics.
You are able to work collaboratively within large, international scientific teams.
You communicate effectively in a scientific environment, including presenting and discussing research results.

title: Transport and Handling Specialist
description:
What you'll do
The Engineering Department (EN) provides CERN with the Engineering expertise, Infrastructure Systems and Technical Coordination necessary for the design, installation, operation, maintenance and dismantling phases of the CERN accelerator complex and its experimental facilities.

The position is within the Transport and Handling Engineering Group (EN-THE), responsible for preparing, organizing and coordinating all transport and handling operations for the CERN accelerators and experiments. The Group also manages the transport of thousands of conventional and unconventional items, chemical and radioactive products each year.

As a Transport and Handling Specialist in EN-THE, you will be part of the Heavy Handling (EN-HE-HH) Section, which is in charge for organising and supervising transport, handling and lifting operations at CERNs accelerators complex, experimental areas and industrial buildings both underground and in surface premises.
Learn more
Your responsibilities
Coordinating transport and handling operations for the Accelerator complex, Experiments, and surface premises.
Coordinating and planning meetings to evaluate technical and resource needs.
Assessing and proposing possible handling and transport solutions.
Defining technical and safety requirements for the transport of dangerous goods and ensuring compliance with ADR principles and applicable regulations.
Specific operations by using customized equipment, analysing related working procedures and Safety assessments.
Developing technical specifications, work procedures and contract documentation for transport and handling activities.
Supervising contractor activities on site, ensuring Safety during the operations in both conventional and radioactive environments.
Collaborating with the EN-THE design office to develop custom handling tools and conduct logistic studies.
Collaborating with Radiation Protection Services to establish/redact the Work Dose Planning and Radiological work permit (DIMR).
Performing handling operations in specific situations.
Still here?
Let's make a quick check about
Your profile
Extensive experience in heavy handling and transport operations.
Proven experience in worksite logistics.
Proven experience in technical contract supervision.
Proven experience of work in a radioactive environment will be an asset.
Basic knowledge of remote-handling systems.
A thorough understanding of the principles of ADR regulations in order to identify, interpret and communicate the requirements applicable to the transport of dangerous goods would be an asset.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Logistics, Mechanics or Electromechanics or a related field.
ADR certificate would be an additional asset. Driving and operator licences for electrical overhead travelling cranes, industrial trucks, mobile elevating platforms, etc would be an additional asset.
Your skills
Operation and maintenance of lifting and handling equipment.
Operation and maintenance of transport systems.
Definition and installation of transport systems.
Transport of dangerous goods.
Delivers high quality work on time and fulfils expectations.
Adapts quickly and resourcefully to shifting priorities and requirements.
Anticipates obstacles; assesses alternative solutions in order to have a fall-back plan.

Follows rules and regulations and encourages others to do the same.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.

A valid driving licence.
Interventions in underground installations.
Participation in a regular stand-by duty, including nights, Sundays and official holidays.
Work in Radiation Areas.
Shift work, when required by the needs of the Organization.
Stand-by duty, when required by the needs of the Organization.

In addition, you will receive important information both before and after your arrival to ensure a smooth transition into your new role. This process is designed to help you get acquainted with CERN’s environment, your team, and the tools and systems you’ll be using.
How big would the team be?

The size of the team you'll be working with at CERN depends on the specific role and department. Some teams are small and highly specialized, while others are larger and more interdisciplinary. During the interview process, you'll have the opportunity to learn more about the team structure for the position you are applying for.
What is the working language at CERN?

The working languages at CERN are English and French. However, it is not always mandatory to speak both languages to work at CERN. We offer language training to help you acquiring the other language.
What support does CERN provide for relocation?

CERN does not offer direct assistance with relocation. However, depending on your role and specific criteria, you may be eligible for certain benefits such as an installation allowance and coverage of travel expenses to join CERN. These benefits are designed to help ease the transition when relocating to the Geneva area. For more information, please consult the “Salary, Benefits and Support“ page.
Do I need a visa to work at CERN?

Whether you need a visa to work at CERN depends on your nationality and the duration of your stay. CERN assists with the necessary visa and work permit processes for its employees and visitors. The specific requirements will be communicated to you during the recruitment process.
What would my salary be?

Salaries at CERN are determined by a structured scale. Salaries are based on your role, qualifications, and experience, and are not subject to negotiation. Specific details will be provided as your application progresses. For more information, please refer to the dedicated page.
